I am seventy years old and have worked this land for forty years. My family has seven mouths, and some of my children have jobs in the city, so I do not have many young hands at home. I have 34.1 mu of good flat land with a reliable well, and I know the wheat-maize rotation as well as I know my own name. I do not gamble with new methods at my age.

For the winter wheat, I will rotary till the stubble after the maize comes off, then sow around the eighth of October with an improved variety like Luyuan 502. I will spread about 100 jin of compound fertilizer per mu as a base, and topdress once with urea in spring when the wheat turns green. Water is precious, so I will irrigate three times: once at sowing if the soil is dry, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. I will spray for weeds once and for insects once or twice. Last year I got 1,100 jin per mu; this year I expect about 1,050 jin per mu if the weather holds.

For the summer maize, I will plant Denghai 605 right after the wheat harvest in early June, sowing directly into the stubble without tilling. It is a hybrid seed that I buy from the dealer every year, and it gives steady yields. I will put down about 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu at sowing and leave it at that — maize does not need topdressing if the base is good. I will irrigate twice, once at sowing and once at the trumpet stage. The corn borer is my main worry, so I will spray twice for insects and once for weeds. I expect about 1,150 jin per mu.

I farm the way my neighbors and I have always done. I trust what my eyes have seen over four decades.
